title: South Koreans Pick Japan for 'Babymoon' Shopping
paragraphs: A "babymoon" is a trip that people take before their baby is born. In the past, many South Korean couples went on babymoons to relax. But now, more and more expectant parents are going to Japan to go shopping for baby products, according to a report in the Korean newspaper Hankook Ilbo.

In the past, popular places for babymoons were Guam and Southeast Asia. In Japan, Okinawa was the most popular place to go. But now, many couples prefer big cities such as Tokyo, Osaka and Fukuoka. Japan is close to Korea, so the flight is short. Also, many Koreans like Japanese food.

One of the most popular stores for Korean parents is Akachan Honpo, a famous Japanese store for baby products. Parents can buy things that are hard to find in Korea, such as some kinds of strollers and high chairs. There are also many baby products with cute characters.

Shopping in Japan can also save money. The Japanese yen is weak, and foreign tourists can get a tax refund. Kim Ji-young, 27, went to Fukuoka when she was 20 weeks pregnant. "There were baby products that aren't available in Korea, and I was also able to get a tax refund," she said.
Lee Eun-hee, a professor at Inha University, said that baby products are becoming more expensive. So, young parents search for good products at reasonable prices.

Bringing large products home can be difficult, though. Some parents buy special packing materials in Japan to protect their shopping. Others put wheels under their boxes to move them to the airport more easily. On social media in Korea, there are now many posts and videos about shopping for baby products in Japan.
